title: agentgateway/agentgateway — Next Generation Agentic Proxy for AI Agents and MCP servers
content:
Agentgateway is an open source proxy built on AI-native protocols (MCP & A2A) that provides drop-in security, observability, and governance for agent-to-LLM, agent-to-tool, and agent-to-agent communication across any framework and environment.
- 
LLM Gateway 
Route traffic to major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and more) through a unified OpenAI-compatible API with budget and spend controls, prompt enrichment, load balancing, and failover.
- 
MCP Gateway 
Connect LLMs to tools and external data sources via MCP with tool federation, stdio/HTTP/SSE/Streamable HTTP transports, OpenAPI integration, and OAuth authentication.
- 
A2A Gateway 
Enable secure agent-to-agent communication using A2A, with capability discovery, modality negotiation, and task collaboration.
- 
Inference Routing 
Intelligent routing to self-hosted models using Kubernetes Inference Gateway extensions, with decisions based on GPU utilization, KV cache, LoRA adapters, and queue depth.
- 
Guardrails 
Multi-layered content filtering with regex, OpenAI moderation, AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Google Model Armor, and custom webhooks.
- 
Security & Observability 
Auth (JWT, API keys, OAuth), fine-grained RBAC with CEL policy engine, rate limiting, TLS, and OpenTelemetry metrics/logs/tracing.
- Standalone Quickstart — Get started with agentgateway in minutes.
- Kubernetes Quickstart — Deploy on Kubernetes using the built-in controller and Gateway API.
Depending on your deployment environment, check out the following docs:
- agentgateway.dev/docs: For deployments without the full Kubernetes controller, driven by flat yaml config.
- agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest: For Kubernetes-based deployments using the built-in Kubernetes controller and Gateway API support.
Agentgateway has a built-in UI for you to explore agentgateway connecting agent-to-agent or agent-to-tool:
Thank you to our sponsors for helping to fund the development of agentgateway!
For instructions on how to contribute to the agentgateway project, see the CONTRIBUTION.md file.
To join a community meeting, add the agentgateway calendar to your Google account. Then, you can find event details on the calendar.
Recordings of the community meetings will be published on our google drive.
agentgateway is currently in active development. If you'd like a feature that's missing, open an issue in our GitHub repo.
Thanks to all contributors who are helping to make agentgateway better.
Agentgateway is a Linux Foundation project.

report.summary: agentgateway is an open-source proxy for AI agents, unifying LLM, MCP, and A2A communication with security, observability, and governance.
report.background: The rapid rise of AI agents has created a fragmented landscape where agents need to talk to LLMs, tools, and each other. Protocols like Anthropic's MCP (Model Context Protocol) and Google's A2A (Agent2Agent) aim to standardize these interactions, but managing security, observability, and cost across diverse frameworks remains challenging. Enterprises struggle with routing, authentication, and policy enforcement. Existing LLM gateways like LiteLLM focus on model routing, but lack native support for agentic protocols. agentgateway, a Linux Foundation project, emerges as a vendor-neutral solution to unify LLM, MCP, and A2A traffic, offering drop-in governance for agent-to-LLM, agent-to-tool, and agent-to-agent communication, backed by major sponsors and active development.
key_points: Unified gateway for LLM, MCP, and A2A: Routes traffic to major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock) via an OpenAI-compatible API with budget controls, load balancing, and failover. Connects LLMs to tools using MCP with federation, multiple transports (stdio/HTTP/SSE), OpenAPI integration, and OAuth. Enables secure agent-to-agent communication via A2A with capability discovery and task collaboration.

Security and observability: Provides authentication (JWT, API keys, OAuth), fine-grained RBAC with a CEL policy engine, rate limiting, TLS, and OpenTelemetry metrics/logs/tracing. Multi-layered guardrails include regex, OpenAI moderation, AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Google Model Armor, and custom webhooks, ensuring content safety and compliance.

Intelligent inference routing: Routes to self-hosted models using Kubernetes Inference Gateway extensions, making decisions based on GPU utilization, KV cache, LoRA adapters, and queue depth. This optimizes resource usage, reduces latency, and lowers costs for production AI workloads.

Kubernetes-native and standalone deployment: Offers a standalone quickstart with flat YAML config for non-Kubernetes environments, and a Kubernetes quickstart with a built-in controller and Gateway API support. As a Linux Foundation project, it ensures vendor-neutral governance and community-driven development.

Open source and community-driven: Active development with a built-in UI for exploring agent-to-agent or agent-to-tool connections. Community meetings, contribution guidelines, and sponsor funding support the project. Missing features can be requested via GitHub issues, encouraging rapid iteration.
report.impact: For the AI industry, agentgateway addresses fragmentation by providing a standardized, secure gateway for agentic protocols, potentially accelerating enterprise adoption of multi-agent systems. It competes with LiteLLM, Portkey, and Envoy AI Gateway, but its native MCP and A2A support differentiates it. Developers gain a drop-in solution for routing, security, and observability, reducing boilerplate and enabling focus on agent logic. However, they must adopt MCP and A2A protocols. Regular users benefit indirectly through more reliable, secure, and cost-effective AI agents, though the infrastructure is invisible. Linux Foundation backing could make it a de facto standard, influencing how agents communicate and are governed.
report.tools: To follow up, try the agentgateway quickstart on GitHub and explore its built-in UI. Learn about MCP and A2A protocols via their official specs. Compare with LiteLLM, Portkey, and Envoy AI Gateway. For Kubernetes, check Gateway API and Inference Gateway extensions. Use OpenTelemetry for observability. Other related tools: Istio, Envoy, and OAuth providers.
